behavior: A checkout running the development Compose file initializes a PostgreSQL role using a public default and supplies its matching DSN to migration/API containers.
input_boundary: Developer launches Compose without overrides. The host database port binds loopback. The backend network and local host are inside this development trust boundary.
evidence: Development server, loopback publishing and backend-only database network are explicit in Compose. A local process or peer on the backend network can use the default. Production Compose has independent deployment configuration.
verification: Compose and production configuration traced. Deployment contract checks cover Compose startup and isolation.
remaining: Sonar owner to distinguish the intentionally usable local credential from a production leak. No disposition or risk acceptance recorded.

behavior: Writes the generated development DSN into worktree runtime configuration for Compose and local harness use.
input_boundary: Local CLI setup owns the worktree and runtime files. Database name and ports derive from local configuration. Network and worktree access are prerequisites.
evidence: write_runtime protects the local directory/files and selects development mode. The value authenticates to that local role, so filesystem privacy alone does not make it a real secret or isolate same-host clients.
verification: Harness runtime writer, generated Compose and direct API environment traced.
remaining: Sonar owner to review the dev-only context per issue.

behavior: Reads and validates a Trivy v2 report and writes sanitized JSON back to the same selected report file.
input_boundary: CI owns the runner-local report directory and only the local CLI caller selects a directory. Scanner-produced JSON is data. Redaction inherits runner filesystem permissions.
evidence: The glob and operator path select the file before parsing. ArtifactName, Target and other JSON fields never select the write target. A locally supplied directory or writable filesystem links require a trusted filesystem context, with no remote report-data path to choose a destination.
verification: Trivy tests cover redaction, secondary platforms, custom filenames and upload only after redaction.
remaining: Propose issue-specific False Positive for the tracked JSON-to-path claim.

behavior: Passes a default verifying client SSLContext to SMTP.starttls before login or message delivery.
input_boundary: The operator supplies SMTP host and settings. Email verification and password reset services pass messages. TLS-enabled delivery requires a peer with a trusted matching certificate.
evidence: Default context enforces certificate validation and hostname matching. STARTTLS failure exits before login/send. Production previously allowed the separate opt-out in N01. No certificate or hostname validation defect in the flagged call.
action: Preserve verifying STARTTLS. Strengthen coverage and fix the separate production opt-out in N01.
verification: test_send_text_email_uses_verifying_tls_context checks real SSLContext flags via a fake SMTP transport.
remaining: Propose issue-specific False Positive for S4830; N01 is tracked independently.

behavior: Pipes a local HTTP health response to fixed Python code using json.load; success requires the ready field.
input_boundary: Hosted production-image smoke starts the repository-built API on the runner network. Only that response body flows to stdin. The workflow owns the source and interpreter invocation.
evidence: The Python program is a literal -c argument. stdin is consumed as JSON data; no interpreter or shell reads the downloaded bytes as source. A malformed or non-ready response fails that probe.
verification: Deployment contract test covers the gate ordering and CI smoke path. Inspected runner-loopback URL and fixed program.
remaining: Propose issue-specific False Positive for downloaded-code execution.

behavior: Runs a repository-owned Python executable and this script with the original CLI arguments after the script argument.
input_boundary: Local operator owns the checkout and venv and invokes an allowed command. The executable must exist and the process must be outside that venv. Local CLI arguments carry the caller's authority.
evidence: Absolute interpreter and script paths come from repository paths. The command is a list and shell defaults to false. CLI options after the script are application arguments. A malicious local replacement of the venv or repository is outside this boundary.
verification: Traced helper entry, venv guard, Windows/POSIX test/check branch and fallback callers. Canonical checks exercise re-execution.
remaining: Propose issue-specific False Positive for command injection at this call.

behavior: Supplies the character membership set for the shared registration and reset password-policy predicate.
input_boundary: Registration and password reset validate user input against a public policy constant before hashing and persistence.
evidence: The predicate iterates user-supplied characters. Hashing uses a random salt and the supplied password, independently of the policy constant.
verification: Inspected auth and password-reset callers and existing test_passwords.py policy tests.
remaining: Propose issue-specific False Positive for a credential literal.

behavior: Sets a synthetic password for the PostgreSQL service used by the production-image CI smoke job.
input_boundary: An ephemeral hosted runner, its PostgreSQL service and the smoke containers share this test configuration. APP_ENV is production for compatibility checks.
evidence: The CI service and generated smoke environment use the same value on the runner. No deployed database or production credential store participates.
verification: CI service, env-file and smoke migration declarations traced. Covered by production-gate contract test.
remaining: Sonar owner to review this per-issue fixture disposition.

behavior: Sets the public local PostgreSQL bootstrap password in a generated runtime environment.
input_boundary: Requires local harness setup and access to the development database from the local machine or backend network.
evidence: Same generated development configuration as F02, but the flagged literal is the environment field used by PostgreSQL rather than the DSN. It is usable within the development boundary.
verification: Traced write_runtime through generated env and Compose consumers.
remaining: Sonar owner to review this per-issue local configuration disposition.

behavior: Read permission was inherited by both the gate and finalizer although Actions API reads occur only in the reusable workflow.
input_boundary: GitHub confirmed disabled_manually. If re-enabled, PR comment events reach the gate with its token before collaborator validation.
evidence: The gate calls collaborator, PR, comment and check endpoints. The finalizer updates a check. The pinned reusable workflow declares actions:read for its read jobs.
action: Move Actions read permission to the reusable-workflow caller job.
verification: Workflow token regression failed on inherited permission and passes with explicit job maps.
remaining: Keep disabled state verified. Validate through ordinary scanner refresh; an operational re-enable requires the workflow owner.

behavior: Statuses read was inherited by jobs that create/update checks and comments without reading commit statuses.
input_boundary: Same disabled workflow and hosted token boundary as F10.
evidence: The pinned reusable workflow declares statuses:read. Gate uses check-run APIs rather than status endpoints; finalizer only updates one check run.
action: Move statuses read to the reusable-workflow caller job.
verification: Workflow token regression and pinned reusable job permissions inspected.
remaining: Validate on main after merge. Workflow remains disabled.

behavior: PR write was inherited by the check-only finalizer.
input_boundary: Same disabled workflow and hosted token boundary as F10. The gate requires write/maintain/admin for actual review triggering.
evidence: The gate posts PR issue comments and the pinned review workflow publishes review feedback. The separate finalizer calls only checks.update.
action: Grant PR write only to the gate and reusable-workflow caller.
verification: Workflow token regression and gate/reusable API consumers inspected.
remaining: Validate on main after merge. Workflow remains disabled.

behavior: Check write was granted at workflow scope rather than at each job needing it.
input_boundary: Same disabled workflow and hosted token boundary as F10.
evidence: All three current jobs need checks write for create/update or reusable reporting. The fix makes each grant explicit with an empty default for future jobs.
action: Grant checks write explicitly to the three current jobs.
verification: Workflow token regression verifies default denial and each job's intended grant.
remaining: Validate on main after merge. Workflow remains disabled.

behavior: Reads a liveness response over HTTP from an ephemeral API container published on host loopback.
input_boundary: Security workflow supplies the freshly built image, Docker maps the host port, and the runner shell selects the endpoint.
evidence: The port publish uses 127.0.0.1 and curl sends neither credentials nor customer data. The request is a local smoke check and compares a fixed liveness body. This assumes the intended local Docker context and hosted runner.
verification: Production runtime verification contract and command traced.
remaining: Sonar owner to review this per-issue smoke-probe disposition.

behavior: Leaves out a CPU limit on the scanner coverage pod.
input_boundary: The security workflow invokes Trivy config on the fixture directory and verifies a finding. Deployment would require separately applying that fixture.
evidence: The fixture directory is skipped during normal repository policy scans and explicitly scanned as a negative test. No checked-in production deployment applies it.
remaining: Sonar owner to review the deliberate negative-fixture disposition.

behavior: Leaves out a memory limit on the same scanner coverage pod.
input_boundary: Same fixture scanning and deployment prerequisites as F15.
evidence: The YAML and JSON fixtures are required negative inputs. The production manifests do not consume this fixture.
remaining: Sonar owner to review the deliberate negative-fixture disposition.

behavior: Preauthorized a particular LAN host for the Next development origin check even when the operator configured nothing. Copying the example also enabled it.
input_boundary: The Next development server consumes the config, with process environment under operator control. The extra trust applies when the server is reachable from an origin at that address.
evidence: The address is private and the setting is development-only. It is still a blanket default for an unrelated network address, which is not stable across developers. Existing explicit overrides already support intentional LAN testing.
action: Remove implicit LAN allowlisting from the config and example. Keep explicit LAN opt-in.
verification: Node config regression failed for the unset variable before the fix and passes after it; explicit multi-host normalization still passes.
remaining: Validate original rule on main after merge.

behavior: A production operator could configure an SMTP host and disable STARTTLS, including with a boolean spelling parsed as false.
input_boundary: Production environment is operator-owned. Cleartext had to be enabled by configuration and a relay accepting plaintext. Reset and verification email bodies may contain bearer tokens.
evidence: SMTP login and send followed the optional TLS branch. Local sink behavior is documented; production had no guard. No evidence was gathered about any live deployment settings.
action: Reject production SMTP configurations that enable delivery without verifying STARTTLS. Keep disabled or development/test mail valid.
verification: Two baseline failures. Six regression cases pass after the change plus the real SSLContext flag test.
remaining: Correct any production configuration using plaintext before rollout. Live configuration was not inspected.
